HtmlAnswer:
To implement Enhanced Input in a custom APlayerController in Unreal Engine 5.6, you must interface with the UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem to register your mappings and use the UEnhancedInputComponent to bind hardware events to logic.

1. Module Setup

Open your project’s .Build.cs file and ensure the “EnhancedInput” module is included in your dependencies:

PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[] { "Core", "CoreUObject", "Engine", "InputCore", "EnhancedInput" });

2. Header File (MyPlayerController.h)

Define the pointers for your input assets and the callback functions. We use EditDefaultsOnly so these can be assigned in a Blueprint subclass of this controller.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "GameFramework/PlayerController.h"
#include "InputActionValue.h"
#include "MyPlayerController.generated.h"

UCLASS()
class MYPROJECT_API AMyPlayerController : public APlayerController
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

protected:
	virtual void BeginPlay() override;
	virtual void SetupInputComponent() override;

	/** Mapping Context containing the IA to Key bindings */
	UPROPERTY(EditDefaultsOnly, Category = "Input")
	class UInputMappingContext* DefaultMappingContext;

	/** Input Action for Movement (WASD / Stick) */
	UPROPERTY(EditDefaultsOnly, Category = "Input")
	class UInputAction* MoveAction;

	/** Input Action for Looking (Mouse / Stick) */
	UPROPERTY(EditDefaultsOnly, Category = "Input")
	class UInputAction* LookAction;

	/** Callback for Move Action */
	void Move(const FInputActionValue& Value);

	/** Callback for Look Action */
	void Look(const FInputActionValue& Value);
};

3. Source File (MyPlayerController.cpp)

In BeginPlay, we retrieve the local player’s input subsystem to inject our context. In SetupInputComponent, we bind the actions to our functions.

#include "MyPlayerController.h"
#include "EnhancedInputComponent.h"
#include "EnhancedInputSubsystems.h"
#include "GameFramework/Pawn.h"

void AMyPlayerController::BeginPlay()
{
	Super::BeginPlay();

	// Add the Mapping Context to the Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem
	if (ULocalPlayer* LocalPlayer = GetLocalPlayer())
	{
		if (UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem* Subsystem = ULocalPlayer::GetSubsystem<UEnhancedInputLocalPlayerSubsystem>(LocalPlayer))
		{
			if (DefaultMappingContext)
			{
				// Priority 0 is base priority. Higher values override lower ones.
				Subsystem->AddMappingContext(DefaultMappingContext, 0);
			}
		}
	}
}

void AMyPlayerController::SetupInputComponent()
{
	Super::SetupInputComponent();

	// Cast the underlying InputComponent to the Enhanced version
	if (UEnhancedInputComponent* EnhancedInputComponent = Cast<UEnhancedInputComponent>(InputComponent))
	{
		// ETriggerEvent::Triggered is used for continuous input (like movement)
		if (MoveAction)
		{
			EnhancedInputComponent->BindAction(MoveAction, ETriggerEvent::Triggered, this, &AMyPlayerController::Move);
		}

		if (LookAction)
		{
			EnhancedInputComponent->BindAction(LookAction, ETriggerEvent::Triggered, this, &AMyPlayerController::Look);
		}
	}
}

void AMyPlayerController::Move(const FInputActionValue& Value)
{
	// Extract the Vector2D value (X for Right/Left, Y for Forward/Backward)
	FVector2D MovementVector = Value.Get<FVector2D>();

	if (APawn* ControlledPawn = GetPawn())
	{
		// Find world-space forward and right vectors based on current controller yaw
		const FRotator Rotation = GetControlRotation();
		const FRotator YawRotation(0, Rotation.Yaw, 0);

		const FVector ForwardDirection = FRotationMatrix(YawRotation).GetUnitAxis(EAxis::X);
		const FVector RightDirection = FRotationMatrix(YawRotation).GetUnitAxis(EAxis::Y);

		// Apply movement
		ControlledPawn->AddMovementInput(ForwardDirection, MovementVector.Y);
		ControlledPawn->AddMovementInput(RightDirection, MovementVector.X);
	}
}

void AMyPlayerController::Look(const FInputActionValue& Value)
{
	// Extract Vector2D for mouse/analog stick looking
	FVector2D LookAxisVector = Value.Get<FVector2D>();

	if (APawn* ControlledPawn = GetPawn())
	{
		// Add yaw (horizontal) and pitch (vertical) to the controller
		AddYawInput(LookAxisVector.X);
		AddPitchInput(LookAxisVector.Y);
	}
}

4. Asset Setup Checklist

To make this code functional in the editor:

  • Input Actions: Create two Input Action assets in Fab or the Content Browser. Set their Value Type to Axis2D (Vector2D).
  • Mapping Context: Create an Input Mapping Context. Add both actions. Map Move to WASD and Look to Mouse XY.
  • Blueprint Child: Create a Blueprint based on AMyPlayerController. Assign the Mapping Context and Input Action assets in the Details panel.
  • Game Mode: Set your Player Controller Class to your new Blueprint in your Game Mode settings.

Best Practices

  • Validation: Always check if DefaultMappingContext and the Subsystem are valid to prevent crashes during initialization.
  • Input Types: Use ETriggerEvent::Triggered for actions that should fire every frame while held (Movement/Looking). For instant actions like Jumping or Elimination triggers, use ETriggerEvent::Started.
  • Subsystems: Using the LocalPlayerSubsystem is preferred over the Pawn-based setup if you want input to persist even if the Pawn is destroyed or swapped.
